problem: The status device (a word-first label such as on track / slipping) and the ledger (a table of logged entries) resolve UNDEFINED although decisions D-10 and D-17 define them exactly. In cadence-dominion both were compiled by hand from docs/synthesis/dominion/decisions.json (gap G13).
insufficiency: resolve('a status label on track or slipping') -> UNDEFINED (closest: component/select 1.0); resolve('a table of logged entries') -> UNDEFINED (no candidates). search('ledger') -> no hits; search('table') -> no hits; search('status label') -> only component/select 1.0. Neither surface exists in the catalogue, so no direct artifact can be cited; the builder could only reach them through the decisions record.
reuse_case: Status words appear in every register/list surface, and the ledger is the system's native form for repeated content (gestalt: documents are the system's native form). cadence-dominion used both — status labels on Today rows and in the achievements tiles; the ledger in History (16 entries, two pages). Any register-style consumer needs the same pair.
composition_check: component/select is a form control, not a label; no table or repeated-content artifact exists; D-17's header rule and row hairlines and D-10's ruled label idiom have no composable catalogue source (the rules/bands live in decisions and tokens, not as a citable pattern). Without the entries, each consumer rebuilds the same register differently — the exact drift the authority exists to prevent.
